chunks: A man said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: “I am the Imam of the mosque of the neighborhood, so I bow with them, and I hear the clattering of their sandals while I am bowing.”
So he said: “Remain in your rukuʿ for the duration of your rukuʿ and the like of your rukuʿ; then if they stop, otherwise stand upright.”

key_terms.إِمَامُ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.رَاكِعٌ: being in the state of rukuʿ, the bowing posture in salat
key_terms.رُكُوعَكَ: your bowing; the Imam’s duration in rukuʿ
key_terms.فَانْتَصِبْ: stand upright, meaning return to the standing posture
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ: the mosque where the congregational prayer is held
key_terms.نِعَالِهِمْ: their sandals, referring to the sound of those arriving

ai.seo_question: May the Imam prolong rukuʿ in congregational salat to allow others to join?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a ruling related to congregational salat when the Imam is in rukuʿ and hears latecomers approaching. It indicates that the Imam may prolong the rukuʿ to a reasonable extent, but should then return to the standing posture if that point has been reached.
